It sets itself apart from standard Fourier-based frequency rendering by avoiding the complexity of handling Hermitian symmetry during slice extraction, which would otherwise be required to save memory in the Fourier domain [S1, S3, unofficial].

The claim states that the method avoids the complexity of handling Hermitian symmetry during slice extraction, which would otherwise be required to save memory in the Fourier domain. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Since the Fourier spectrum of a real signal is hermitian, the same amount of memory saving is possible with the Fourier transform by dropping half of the spectrum... However, such implementation would unnecessarily complicate the slice extraction process.' It further explains that the Hartley transform avoids this by mapping real functions to real spectra directly. Source [S3] notes corroborate this by stating the Hartley transform is preferred over dropping half the Fourier spectrum because dropping half complicates the slice extraction process. Therefore, every fact in the claim is supported by the evidence.
